definitions.gloss: spiriting away, mysterious disappearance attributed to supernatural forces
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese belief that when a person — especially a child — vanished without explanation, they had been hidden away by gods, spirits, or tengu. In modern usage, refers to any sudden, inexplicable disappearance.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{神隠|かみかく}しに{遭|あ}った。
{昔|むかし}は{行方不明|ゆくえふめい}になることを{神隠|かみかく}しと{呼|よ}んだ。
examples.english: In the old days, disappearances were called kamikakushi.

examples.japanese: {村|むら}の{少女|しょうじょ}がある{日|ひ}{突然|とつぜん}{姿|すがた}を{消|け}し、{人々|ひとびと}は{神隠|かみかく}しだと{噂|うわさ}した。
examples.english: A girl from the village suddenly vanished one day, and people whispered that she had been spirited away.

notes:
USAGE:
A word rooted in Japanese folklore. Historically, unexplained disappearances of people — particularly children — were attributed to gods ({神|かみ}) or supernatural beings like {天狗|てんぐ} who would {隠|かく}す (hide) the person. The word became widely known internationally through the Studio Ghibli film {千|せん}と{千尋|ちひろ}の{神隠|かみかく}し (Spirited Away, 2001).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神隠|かみかく}しに{遭|あ}う: to be spirited away
- {神隠|かみかく}しにあったように: as if spirited away
- {千|せん}と{千尋|ちひろ}の{神隠|かみかく}し: Spirited Away (film title)
